trial_name.text: Study 233AS101 Part C (VALOR), noted as Study 101C

citations.quote: The submission contains efficacy, safety, and biomarker results from a single adequate and well-controlled study (Study 233AS101 Part C, noted as Study 101C in this review)
On January 15, 2019, the Applicant submitted a protocol amendment to account for the addition of Part C (VALOR) to Study 233AS101.
confirmed by a central laboratory (Study 1 Part C, NCT02623699).

Study 101C was a Phase 3, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, study of tofersen in adult subjects with ALS and a confirmed pathogenic or likely pathogenic SOD1 mutation (SOD1-ALS).

design.text: 28-week multicenter (32 sites, 9 countries), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized 2:1 to tofersen or placebo, stratified by fast/non-fast progressor

citations.quote: Study 101C was a multicenter (32 study sites), multinational (nine countries), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 3 study of tofersen in adult subjects with SOD1-ALS.
Patients were randomized 2:1 to tofersen or placebo. Randomization was stratified by fast progressor and non-fast progressor.

population.text: Adults (23 to 78 years) with weakness attributable to ALS and a confirmed SOD1 mutation (SOD1-ALS)

citations.quote: The efficacy of QALSODY was assessed in a 28-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical study in patients 23 to 78 years of age with weakness attributable to ALS and a SOD1 mutation confirmed by a central laboratory

endpoint.text: Primary: change from baseline to Week 28 (Day 197) in the ALSFRS-R total score in the mITT population (joint rank test plus multiple imputation)

citations.quote: The primary efficacy analysis was the change from baseline to Week 28 in the ALSFRS-R total score in the mITT population, analyzed using the joint rank test to account for mortality in conjunction with multiple imputation (MI) to account for missing data for withdrawals other than death.

n.text: 108 randomized (72 tofersen, 36 placebo); mITT primary population n=60

citations.quote: the actual number randomized was N=108 (72 to tofersen and 36 to placebo).
The prespecified primary analysis population (n = 60, modified intent to treat [mITT])

result.text: Primary endpoint negative: numerical difference of 1.2 favoring tofersen in ALSFRS-R change at Week 28 (-7.0 tofersen vs -8.1 placebo; joint rank + MI p=0.9689), not statistically significant. Plasma NfL reduced at Week 28 (67% difference in geometric mean ratios tofersen vs placebo, nominal p<0.0001).

citations.quote: There was a numerical difference of 1.2 favoring tofersen in ALSFRS-R change from baseline at Week 28 (-7.0-point decline in the tofersen group and -8.1-point decline in the placebo group; joint rank test plus multiple imputation p=0.9689), but this difference was not statistically significant.

a reduction in plasma NfL, a marker of neuronal degeneration, was observed at Week 28 in the tofersen group compared to the placebo group (67% difference in geometric mean ratios for tofersen to placebo, nominal p<0.0001).

indication.text: QALSODY is indicated for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in adults who have a mutation in the SOD1 gene; approved under accelerated approval based on reduction in plasma NFL.

citations.quote: QALSODY is indicated for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in adults who have a mutation in the superoxide dismutase 1 (*SOD1*) gene. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on reduction in plasma neurofilament light chain (NFL) observed in patients treated with QALSODY

target_moa.text: Tofersen is an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) that binds and degrades SOD1 mRNA to reduce synthesis of the SOD1 protein; gain-of-function SOD1 mutations are thought to cause toxic SOD1 protein aggregates in ALS.

citations.quote: Tofersen is an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) designed to bind and degrade superoxide dismutase (SOD1) mRNA to reduce synthesis of the SOD1 protein.
gain-of-function mutations in SOD1 are thought to cause the formation and accumulation of toxic SOD1 protein aggregates.
Tofersen is an intrathecal ASO that targets the SOD1 mRNA to reduce synthesis of SOD1 protein.
Pharmacologic class	Antisense oligonucleotide

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were pain (42% vs 22% placebo), fatigue (17% vs 6%), arthralgia (14% vs 6%), CSF white blood cell increased (14% vs 0%), and myalgia (14% vs 6%). Serious adverse reactions included myelitis/radiculitis (6 patients), papilledema/elevated intracranial pressure (4 patients), and aseptic meningitis.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge 10% of patients treated with QALSODY and greater than placebo) were pain, fatigue, arthralgia, cerebrospinal fluid white blood cell increased, and myalgia. (6.1)

vote.text: The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee (March 22, 2023) voted unanimously 9 to 0 that the available evidence supports that reduction in NfL is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: A meeting of the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee was held on March 22, 2023. At that meeting, the committee voted unanimously, 9 to 0, that the available evidence supports that a reduction in NfL concentration observed in tofersen-treated patients with SOD1-ALS is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit for these patients.

detail.text: NDA 215887 was submitted May 25, 2022 and approved under accelerated approval effective the date of the letter; no prior CRL is described.

citations.quote: Biogen submitted NDA 215887 for tofersen on May 25, 2022.

citations.quote: The Division has determined that the observed reduction in plasma NfL concentration is acceptable as a surrogate endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in patients with SOD1-ALS.

summary.text: Tofersen received Fast Track (2015) and Orphan Drug designation; a Breakthrough Therapy request was denied. The NDA received Priority review and was granted accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 based on reduction in plasma NfL as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, with a required confirmatory Phase 3 trial (ATLAS).
